summary: Gelek was a scholar in Tibetology. He served as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998) and held posts as a visiting lecturer at the University of California and visiting scholar at the University of Oxford.

Gelek Rinpoche was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Monastery, Young Lamas Home School, and Cornell University. He served as director of Tibet House, New Delhi (1965) and founded Jewel Heart in 1988.

Gembo Dorji is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Tango Buddhist College, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, alongside traditional teachers including Tenzin Dhendrup and Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima.

Gen'ichi Yamazaki was an Indologist and historian who earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He was a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (~1967–1981) and later served as professor at Kokugakuin University in 2006.

Gendun Chopel was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied at Drisha, Kumbum, Labrang, and Drepung monasteries, and his teachers included Gendun Tendzin Gyatso and Sherab Gyatso.
Gendun Chophel worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sherab Gyatso from circa 1921 to 1927 and held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society in 1941.

Gendun Rinpoche was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies figure. He founded Dhagpo Kagyu Ling, Dhagpo Kundreul Ling, Dhagpo Dargye Ling, and Dhagpo Dedrol Ling, and served as abbot and retreat master at Dhagpo Kagyu Ling (~1977–1997).

Genjun Sasaki specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, graduating from Kyoto University. He taught as a professor at Otani University (attested 1974–1995), a Fulbright professor at Harvard, and a visiting professor at the University of Hamburg (1956).
Genro Gito was an 18th-century Buddhist studies figure who succeeded Hakuin Ekaku and served as head monk (第一座) at Myoshin-ji.
Genryu Kagoshima was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and later served there as a professor from circa 1957 to 1983.

Gensho Imanari was a Japanologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from Waseda University. He was an assistant professor at Kokushikan University and later served as professor (1980) and professor emeritus (1996) at Rissho University.
Genshu Watanabe was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University and under Sogaku Daiun Harada, of whom he was a dharma heir.
Genzao worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950 and trained under traditional teachers Jiangze Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche.

Geo Widengren was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies. Educated at Stockholm and Uppsala universities under Henrik Samuel Nyberg, he was professor of religious history at Uppsala (1940–1973) and president of the IAHR (~1960–1970).

Geoff Childs is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who earned his PhD at Indiana University. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at the Australian National University and became assistant professor of anthropology at Washington University in St. Louis.

Geoffrey Barstow specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned degrees from Kathmandu University and the University of Virginia, and became an assistant professor of religious studies at Oregon State University around 2013.

Geoffrey Goble is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned degrees from the University of Virginia and Indiana University, and was appointed assistant professor of religious studies at the University of Oklahoma (attested 2019).

Geoffrey Samuel, a Tibetology and religious studies scholar, earned his PhD from Cambridge. He held professorships at Newcastle and Lancaster, and retired as Emeritus Professor from Cardiff University by 2014.

Georg Buddruss was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate under Paul Thieme at Goethe University Frankfurt and served as professor at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1963–1995).

Georg Bühler was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He held professorships at Elphinstone College, Deccan College, the University of Mumbai, and the University of Vienna.
